headline: Failed resolution would have directed the President to remove US troops from hostilities with Iran unless Congress authorized military force.
what_it_does: This resolution would have directed the President to pull US Armed Forces out of hostilities against Iran unless Congress declared war or passed a specific authorization for military force against Iran. It would not have applied to forces needed to defend the United States, an ally, or a partner from an imminent attack, as long as the President followed a War Powers Resolution rule that generally requires ending such involvement within 60 days without congressional approval. The Senate rejected it 48 to 51 on November 19, 2026.

who_it_affects.how: Troops engaged in hostilities with Iran would have been ordered removed from those hostilities unless Congress authorized the use of force.
The President would have needed a declaration of war or a congressional authorization to continue military action against Iran, except for defense against imminent attacks.

who_it_affects.group: US allies and partners in the region
who_it_affects.how: US forces could still have defended them from imminent attack, subject to the War Powers Resolution's time limits.
